FOREWORD

o.~ The indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 8 July 1965, after the draft finalized by the Animal Feeds Sectional ~mmittee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council.

0.2 TUR or ARHAR G'HUNI is a common livestock feed in India. The formulation of this standard was undertaken by the Animal Feeds Sectional Committee in accordance with its programme planned for the formulation of Indian-Standards for the various livestock feeds used in this country,
0-' This standard contains a clause (see 4.1) which calls for an agreement between the purchaser and the vendor at the time of placing orders,
t

0.4 FOT the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this s~ndard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, express~_ the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance 'with IS: 2-1960�. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of test for TUR or AJrHAR (CtJjtulUS cojan L. ) GHUNI for use a~ livestock feed.
,

2. GRADES
2.1 TUR or ARHAR CHUNI shall be of two grades, namely, Grade 1" and
Grade 2.

3. ,REQ,UIREMENTS

3.1 Oucriptloa - TUR or ARHAR CHUNI shall be the material obtained as a by-product in the preparation of TUR or ARHAR DAL Cor human consumption and shall consist of finer broken pieces of DAL

The material shall be free from fungus or insect infestation. 3.2 The material shall also conform to the requirements prescribed in

4. PACKING

4.1 t: nless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the vendor, the material shall be packed in sound jute bags. The mouth of each bag shall be either machine-stitched or rolled over and hand-stitched with Itron. jute twine.
5. 'MARKING 5.1 Each bag shall be marked \yitll the following information: a) Namt. and grade of the material t b) Name of the manufacturtr. and c) Net weight in kg.

5.3 Each bag may also be marked with the lSI Certification Mark,
NOD - The \lie of the lSI Certification ~Iark is governed by the provisiODl of the Indian Standarda Jnltitution ( Certification Afarkl ) Act, and the Rule. and ReaulatioDi awle thereunder. Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indian StaDdard conveys the UlUrance that -they have been produced to comply with the requiremeDti that standard, under a weU-defined system of inspection, tnting and quality control dwiq production. This system, which is devised and supervised by lSI and operated by'the producer. has the further saresuard tliat the products as actually marketed are continuously checked by lSI for conformity to the stllndard. I. IAMPUNG AND CRITERIA POR CONFORMITY
1.1 Representative samples of the material for tests shan be drawn accordilll to the method prescribed in Appendix A of IS : 2052�1962-.

&.2 N. .ber 01 T ..t. - Test for crude protein and acid insoluble ash shall be conducted individually on each of the samples constituting a set of test samples while the tests for the remaining characteristics, specified in Table 1, shall be conducted on the composite sample.
6., CrIteria lor Co.I..-mit)' - A lot shall be considered as conforming to the specification, when: a) each of the test results for crude protein .and acid insoluble ash s,tisfies the requirements as specified in Table I J and b) the--test results on the composite sample satisfy the requirements fot..t~t remaining characteristics specified in Table I.

1.3.1..J� .one or more test results do not ..atisfy the requirements for crude protein and acid insoluble ash, the following procedure sball be adopted for detetmliling the conformity of the material for these two characteristics:

---------eSpedicatioD tor......ced reed alamm lor cattle.

Calculate thLmean and range as follows: Mean (X) _ Sum of the test results Number of test samples Range (R) == Difference between the maximum and the minimum values of the test results

IS I 3160 � 1965 The requirements for crude protein and acid insoluble ash shall be considered as fulfilled if: X - 0'4 R is equal to or greater than the requirement Ifor crude protein, and X + 0'4 R is less than or equal to the requirement for acid insoluble ash.

-

6.3.2 If the requirements for all the remaining characteristics are not satisfied after testing the composite sample, a test or tests for the characteristic(s) not satisfyin~ the requirement(s) shan be made on each of the test samples in the set. If the test results obtained on each of the individual samples satisfy the requirement(s) of the specification for the relevant characteristic(s), then the lot shall be considered as having satisfied the requlrement(s) in respect of such characteristic (5) . 7. TESTS

A-I. PROCEDURE
A-I.l Weigh accurately about 2 g of the dried t material (SI' 0.2.1 of IS : 2052.1962* ) in a tared porcelain, silica or platinum dish. Ignite with the flame of a Meker burner for about one hour. <::Omplete the ignition by keeping in a mufHe furnace at 600� � 20�0 until grey ash results. Cool in a desiccator and weigh. Ignite th~ dish again in the muffle furnace for
